newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates mixed, spots mostly up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates mixed, spots mostly up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed on Tuesday with heavy institutional selling pushing early-maturing contracts sharply lower, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded three-day contract fell to 2.50 percent from 4.15 percent on Monday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell to 1.72 million lots from 2.24 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"Short-term fund demand fell sharply, which pushed down the rates," said one trader.
"The short rates are likely to linger around current levels in the next few days as there are no new A share issues on the stock market this week," he added.
New stock issues have routinely added to demand for short-term funds.
But the long-term contracts rose on a technical rebound after sharp losses over the past few weeks, traders said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Tuesday in very active trading led by the two longest contracts, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 112.50 yuan from 111.84 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose to 1.27 million lots from 820,281 lots.
Traders said institutions borrowed heavily on Tuesday which pushed both prices and volumes up.
They said they expected the rebound to extend over the next few days due to sufficient supplies of funds and an uncertain short-term outlook on the stock markets.
